Episode 257. The Demon Army' Attack (8)
While Rondo was gritting his teeth, someone approached his side and shrugged. It was a woman wearing a white mask and a hood.
“Number 677, this world is truly special in many ways, Lord Rondo.”
“...Lord Silyn, when did you arrive?”
Silyn Zipple; she was a first-class executive of the Demon Army. Although Rondo, a special-class executive, was of a higher rank, he cautiously watched Silyn's expression.

He had no choice. It was only because Silyn was not of the direct lineage that her rank was low; there were extremely few people within the Demon Army who had achieved more merits than she. Even Rondo, who had traveled through numerous dimensions and successfully completed wars of conquest, was no match for her.
Rondo considered Silyn to be, in effect, in a position to evaluate and supervise him.
“I arrived a little while ago. Since you requested support from all dimensions.”
“Ah.”
“They are truly powerful enemies. I too have experienced quite a few wars, but this is the first time I have seen those who resist so meaningfully and fiercely.”
“That is correct. Lord Kelliark had seen through it all correctly from the beginning, to the point where I am ashamed of myself for not understanding it right away at the meeting that day.”
“I don't think you need to think that way. It is only natural that he is far ahead of us. It is a relief that you have made the right judgment now.”
To Rondo's ears, those words were a warning. A warning that, as he had made the 'right judgment,' he would have to pay the price if this endeavor were to fail.

“...Although we have lost numerous troops due to a stronger resistance than expected, the atmosphere is not as bad as it seems. Chiron's sword is dying down, and while there is the Battle God Van, I do not think that she will be able to suppress our forces more strongly than Chiron.”
“Is that really so?”

“Even if Van were to display a combat power greater than Chiron's, that is as far as it goes. We have four times more troops remaining than we have lost, and they are continuously being replenished. Above all, since even you have come, Lord Silyn, how could they possibly turn this around?”
“Hmm, that's strange.”
“What do you mean by strange?”
“The Lord Rondo I knew was surely more brilliant than this. I wonder if you are speaking so complacently because you are conscious of me.”
A chill ran down Rondo's spine at Silyn's calm voice. However, Rondo soon composed himself and met Silyn's eyes. The black pupils beyond the mask were glistening.

“Lord Rondo, the enemies have reached the final legacy of Solderet. That is a legacy that we have not been able to properly confirm in any world. And the enemies will now be able to enter that legacy in four and a half days.”
“...Four and a half days?”
“It means we do not have much time.”
Four and a half days; Rondo wondered if his fleet could finish off the enemies within that time. It seemed possible enough, but he could not be certain.

“In the first place, it seems you did not know this information until I arrived, Lord Rondo, so how could you speak so complacently? Before being conscious of me, it seems your reason has already been somewhat paralyzed by fear.”
While the worst possible evaluation continued, Silyn lightly patted Rondo's shoulder as if to relieve his tension.

“But the decision to push the troops in as arrow fodder was very well done. Since time is not entirely on our side, investing troops unconditionally was the best move. Even if it was extremely inefficient.”
Soon, Rondo inwardly breathed a sigh of relief.
“That is a relief. By the way, Lord Silyn, do you have other business to attend to?”
“That is correct. I have to deliver some information to you, so I responded to the summons for now.”
She has other business.

The reason why the key figures of the Demon Army, including Rondo, revered Silyn was because she was the person who had achieved the most merits in subjugating 'rebels,' in addition to wars of conquest. There had been those who had resisted across all dimensions like the Demon Army, not just figures who had fought only in their respective worlds like Orgal of each dimension.

They mainly operated passively, coming and going through the passages between dimensions, but tracking those passages was a mission far more dangerous than a war of conquest. Because if one made a mistake, one could become trapped in the infinite space of a dimensional passage, unable to either die or live.
It was very rare for anyone to succeed more than three times in a dimensional passage chase, but Silyn had a record of succeeding hundreds of times.
“...It seems the remnants have finally shown themselves.”
“Yes, I must find and eliminate that person from now on. So unless his movements are deeply related to this war, I will not be participating in the battle directly.”
“Understood. The remaining time of four and a half days and the appearance of the rebels... is there any other information you can give me besides that?”
“The state of Lord Kelliark's recovery is the last.”
“Has his recovery finished!?”

“No. He said it would be finished in about five days. Four and a half days, five days. The fact that the time Lord Kelliac recovers and the time the enemies reach the legacy are almost the same... isn't it strange? To the point where it feels like some unseen something is helping the enemies.”
Rondo nodded heavily. The phenomena of luck and coincidence were unusually favorable to the 677th dimension.

Kelliark would not be participating in this war. In the first place, Rondo had not been counting on his direct participation, but it did mean that one thing he could have hoped for if the situation were to be overturned had been reduced.
“I will fight with that in mind.”
“Yes, then I shall now trust in you, Lord Rondo, and be on my way.”
Chiron's ultimate technique ended, and twelve more hours passed after that. Exactly one day had passed since the battle began.

The battle did not enter a lull for even a single moment even after Realm of Emptiness disappeared. A fierce, intense battle continued without a second's rest, and now, casualties were beginning to occur in earnest on the coalition's side as well.
“Haah, haah, heok...!”

Vanessa looked ahead, panting for breath. She could see an Elona of the Holy Army, her entire body bound in restraints. Number 45, the eighth Elona that the coalition's superhumans had succeeded in sealing.
“Vanessa, are you alright?”
“It seems I've gotten old. My body won't listen to me.”
“It's just that you can't help it, as you've been fighting nothing but harsh battles ever since the Black Sea.”
Go back to the flagship Sarah for a moment and recover your stamina.
Hedo couldn't bring himself to say those words to Vanessa. More Elonas were still being added now, so if she were to leave her post, the damage to their allies would increase by that much.

Now, the enemy fleet was maintaining over a thousand ships and was encroaching on their front line. They could use the Plutonian Cannon to wipe out the enemies once, but they had to save it as much as possible. Because if they could hold out until the reinforcements and Qwaul arrived without activating it even once, they could increase the maximum number of shots.
Furthermore, firing the Plutonian Cannon now was no different from an act of annihilating their own allies who had infiltrated the enemy lines.
'But if necessary, that too is a choice that cannot be helped.'
Geok, Kwadeudeudeu...!

Suddenly, a dull, deafening roar erupted above Hedo and Vanessa's heads. A golden ship, belonging to the Tikan 3rd Fleet, which had been hit by the magic ray of an enemy Genesis Knight and the main cannon of a white ship, was splitting in half and exploding.
A golden ship of the Tikan 3rd Fleet; it wasn't a flagship, but about fifty coalition members were on board. All of them would meet their deaths without exception.
It was the first time. The first time a golden ship had been completely destroyed and shot down.

Although they had only lost one ship while destroying well over ten thousand enemy ships, just as even the most solid rampart can collapse as a small crack spreads, from now on, the golden ships were bound to continue falling to the ground.
Before even a minute had passed from that, a second golden ship was destroyed, and the sight of a third and a fourth also falling at the same time followed.

The golden ships were literally fighting one against a hundred, but they were slowly reaching their limit. Before the infinity of the white fleets that endlessly emerged from the dimensional gates no matter how many were destroyed.
Hedo and Vanessa naturally advanced a little deeper into the battlefield, avoiding the falling debris of their allies. They could feel the energy of a newly added Elona.
“...I find myself wishing that our leader doesn't know this fact.”
“How could he not know? The Young Patriarch is a Genesis Knight. He must have perceived it even more clearly than us, who were right below the destroyed golden ship.”
That was correct.
'Lord Bran of the Council of Seven. And numerous coalition members have just departed. They are departing...'

Jin was perceiving the deaths of his allies even more accurately than Hedo and Vanessa. The expressions, voices, and attitudes of them as they were swept up in the explosion within the ship felt as if they had happened right in front of him.
That was why everyone was worried about Jin, but he did not show any sign of being distressed or hesitating.
Until the war was completely over.
Not just the war here in the Black Sea, but until the fight against the Demon Army was completely over. All sorrow and guilt had to be buried in the deepest part of his inner self.
Even if it wasn't just a coalition member whose face and name he barely knew, but even if his most beloved ones were to die before his eyes.
Because he was resolved as such, Jin did not go to support Vanessa and the superhumans who were crossing the line between life and death second by second on the battlefield right behind him.
He did not go even when he had a moment of leisure. Because if he had a moment, he should not help the superhumans, but recover even for a moment to prepare to face the next Genesis Knight.
“Charge. If you retreat because the shield has been broken, it is the end! Stick closer to them, tighten the front line even more!”
Soon, as Jin shouted, the Golden Fleet raised new ships to the destroyed first rank and increased its speed.
If they did so, the Plutonian brothers would be the first to die. However, the Plutonians did not find Jin's order uncomfortable. They were people who could die for each other at any time.
“Let's go, brothers!”
The remaining time was now three days.
The time of war was flowing slowly and cruelly for both the Demon Army and the coalition.
